Subject: Azure Marketplace certification invoice & onboarding questions

Hi Hannah / Jonas,

Attached is the invoice from the marketplace onboarding team for the Azure co-sell certification (invoice attached: nova_cert_invoice_0626.pdf). A couple of quick questions as we prepare PO routing on our side: 

- Is the certification fee typically covered by the ISV (Redwood) or split with the merchant for co-sell?
- If split, do you have a standard percentage split or precedent for this class of deal?
- What is the expected timeline from payment to merchant listing (we have a go-live target of Aug 10).

We want to avoid surprises in procurement — can you confirm the required billing contact and whether a single PO to Microsoft on our side is acceptable, or whether we should route charges to Redwood?

Thanks,
Marcus

Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace certification invoice & onboarding questions

Hi Marcus — thanks for sending this over and for the clear timeline. Looping in Jonas and Marissa from our marketplace and commercial ops teams to confirm details.

High level answers up front:
- We can be flexible on the certification fee split but we typically absorb it for strategic co-sell motions where the partner commits to minimum co-sell activity in the first 90 days.
- If we ask the merchant to contribute, a 70/30 Redwood/merchant split is the usual starting point for enterprise listings, but we can negotiate based on ARR and go-live urgency.
- Once payment is processed and Partner Center enrollment is confirmed, typical listing times are 4–6 weeks; we can fast-track to 2–3 weeks if both sides complete required forms ASAP.

Can you confirm:
- Whether NovaMed will raise a PO to Microsoft or to Redwood (PA/PO routing matters for our finance team)
- The legal entity name and billing address you want on the invoice
- Whether you can share the Azure Partner Center org ID or MPN ID (we need this to validate enrollment)

Attached: redwood_onboarding_checklist_v2.xlsx — this lists the minimum artifacts we need to fast-track (MPN, publisher contact, logo assets, security attestation).

If helpful I can jump on a 20-minute call Monday to run through the checklist and next steps.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_onboarding_checklist_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 8 rows)

Marcus / Hannah — quick note from marketplace ops POV. Forwarding Marcus' original email below for context.

Operational proposal:
- Redwood will cover the certification fee up front and invoice NovaMed as a pass-through in the first billing cycle if NovaMed agrees to a 12-month commitment of co-sell registration and a joint GTM plan.
- If NovaMed prefers no Redwood pass-through, we can split 70/30 Redwood/NovaMed. The 70/30 split lets Redwood keep the majority of the first-year placement uplift and keeps merchant onboarding friction low.
- For revenue recognition and procurement: route the cost to Redwood's revenue ops team (revops@redwood.com). We will then issue a single invoice to NovaMed with the certification line item clearly marked — minimizes Azure portal churn.

Required items from NovaMed to accept Redwood -> pay model:
- Signed purchase order referencing DEAL-38921-AZ
- MPN ID + Partner Center org ID
- Billing contact + remit address

If Hannah can confirm we should cover up front, I will ask finance to issue the payment to Microsoft and track recovery. If not, we'll provide guidance for NovaMed to pay Microsoft directly and advise on the merchant-side steps.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head, Marketplace Partnerships
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Hello Hannah and team,

Thanks for the note — copying standard policy and next steps below. We can confirm enrollment once we receive payment and the partner center enrollment details.

Azure Marketplace notes:
- Certification fee is paid to Microsoft and is non-refundable.
- Microsoft does not mandate a specific split between ISV and merchant; that is a commercial arrangement between parties.
- Typical processing: payment + MPN verification -> publisher review -> listing approval (4–6 weeks). Expedited review may be available for verified partners with completed security attestations.

To expedite, please provide the following: 
1) Partner Center Org ID / MPN ID
2) Proof of payment or payment confirmation (if Redwood covers up front)
3) The publisher contact email for listing management

We have attached an invoice stub for your records: mp-enrollment-invoice-stub.pdf. Once payment is processed, notify this alias and include the payment reference so we can move the listing into the enrollment queue.

Best,
Azure Marketplace Partner Operations
mp-ops@microsoft.com

Attachment: mp-enrollment-invoice-stub.pdf (1 page PDF, policy + stub)
